questions.q: What does a router use to decide where to forward a packet?
options: The destination IP address and its routing table
questions.explain: A router works at Layer 3. It matches the destination IP address against its routing table to choose the next hop.

questions.q: What does the code S* mean in show ip route?
questions.explain: S means static and * marks a candidate default route, which is the 0.0.0.0/0 route.

questions.q: The destination is 10.1.2.50. The matching routes are 10.0.0.0/8, 10.1.0.0/16, 10.1.2.0/24 and 0.0.0.0/0. Which route is used?
questions.explain: Longest Prefix Match: among the matching routes, the one with the longest prefix (/24) wins.

questions.q: Which network and prefix make up the default route?
questions.explain: 0.0.0.0/0 matches any destination and is used only when no other route matches.

questions.q: Which command adds a static route to 192.168.3.0/24 through the next hop 10.0.12.2?
As a packet moves from router to router (without NAT), what changes?
options: The source and destination IP addresses
The MAC addresses in the frame
questions.explain: Every hop builds a new frame with new MAC addresses. The IP addresses stay the same.

questions.q: What is the default administrative distance of a static route?
A ping request reaches PC-C, but no reply comes back. What is the most likely cause?
options: A missing return route toward PC-A's network
The type of cable being used
The IP address is in a private range
questions.explain: Routes are needed in both directions. The reply cannot return if a router on the way has no route to PC-A's network.
